newsitem.title: USA: Steris to buy Bristol-Myers Calgon assets.
newsitem.headline: Steris to buy Bristol-Myers Calgon assets.

text.p: Steris Corp. said Wednesday it will buy the infection and contamination control business of Calgon Vestal Laboratories Inc. from Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. for $75 million in cash.

The business competes in the $1.3 billion global market for instrument cleaning and decontamination, antimicrobial and routine hand washing cleansers, hard surface disinfectants and surgical scrubs used by healthcare providers, Steris said.

Steris, which provides surgical and infection prevention products, said one of its main goals has been to expand the consumable part of its product line to include surface cleaners, decontaminants, disinfectants and sterilants.

"After the acquisition, revenues from consumables and services will account for more than 45 percent of Steris' total business," said Bill Sanford, Steris' chairman, president, and chief executive officer.
Steris has about 3,500 employees worldwide, including more than 1,000 direct sales, service, and field support personnel.
The deal is expected to close by the end of December.
Mentor, Ohio-based Steris' stock edged down 12.5 cents to $35.75 early on Nasdaq. Bristol-Myers fell 50 cents to $114 on the New York Stock Exchange.
